header.name: Applied Multivariate Analysis (AMA)
header.description: This course will cover a range of models and methodologies for analyzing multivariate data. It will focus on analysis, interpretation, and understanding of datasets involving multiple variables. The multivariate normal distribution will be studied in detail, along with one-way and two-way MANOVA. Commonly used multivariate techniques, including Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Factor Analysis, Canonical Correlation Analysis, Classification, and Clustering, will be explored. The emphasis will be on applying these methods to real-world datasets and interpreting the resulting findings.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to analyze and make inferences on multivariate data

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to build statistical models used for multivariate data, distinguish and apply feature selection methodologies, learn to implement some supervised and unsupervised multivariate data analysis techniques

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to build codes in R (or equivalent) to analyze and build multivariate statistical models and make interpretations

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to apply analyze the real life multivariate data sets.

lecture_topics: Basics of matrices and random vectors
properties of mean vectors and covariance matrices
Multivariate Normal distribution (MVN) - introduction, its properties, maximum likelihood estimation
Sampling distribution of sample mean and sample covariance matrix, their large sample properties
weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: Assignment I : On basics and MVN

lecture_topics: Hotelling's T^2 and likelihood ratio test
Comparing means vectors of two populations
weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: Assignment II : On inferences for means,MANOVA
Assignment III: On regression models, PCA, FA
Assignment IV (time permitting): On related topics
